messages.content: Search English Wikipedia for each sub-question in parallel, retrieving the most relevant pages.

I'm ready to run the parallel Wikipedia searches, but the request doesn't actually contain a research topic or any sub-questions — the message only includes the instruction to search, with no subject matter to search for.

If I were to invoke the research tool now, I'd have to invent questions arbitrarily, which would produce a report on a topic you never asked about. To execute this properly, I need one of the following:

1. **A main research topic** — I can then decompose it into 2–5 focused, non-overlapping sub-questions and dispatch them to parallel research agents in a single batch.
2. **An explicit list of sub-questions** — I'll pass them directly to the parallel research tool as-is (batched appropriately if there are more than 5).

Once you supply the topic or sub-questions, my workflow will be:

- **Batch dispatch**: All independent sub-questions go out in one parallel call (up to 10 accepted; larger batches are queued or rejected, so I'd split them into batches of ≤5–10).
- **Source-grounded synthesis**: Each agent searches English Wikipedia and returns relevant pages/snippets — no answers from memory alone.
- **Cited report**: I consolidate findings into a comprehensive report with numbered citations [1], [2], etc., mapped back to the Wikipedia pages retrieved.

Please provide the topic or sub-question list, and I'll run the searches immediately.
